sec: Incidentaloma, cardiac effects and first investigations · p855

items.q: Among benign adrenal incidentalomas, the functional tumour order is:
items.exp: Benign (m/c) incidentalomas are endocrine-inactive or functional; functional: cortisol-producing > pheochromocytoma. (Book p855)

items.q: The alarm signs in a NON-functioning adrenal tumour prompting adrenalectomy (any one) are:
opts: Size >4 cm, CT density >20 HU, CT contrast washout <40%
items.exp: Alarm signs: size >4 cm; CT density >20 HU; CT contrast washout <40% — any 1 (+) → adrenalectomy. (Book p855)

items.q: Catecholamine excess affects the heart by raising:
opts: Rate, excitability, O2 consumption and force
items.exp: Heart: ↑ rate, ↑ excitability, ↑ O2 consumption, ↑ force. (Book p855)

items.q: Pheochromocytoma is a named cause of which cardiomyopathy (the other being sarcoidosis)?
items.exp: Cause for dilated cardiomyopathy (other cause: sarcoidosis). (Book p855)

items.q: Which is NOT in the book's hypercalcaemia-associated disease list?
items.exp: Listed: Addison's disease, pheochromocytoma, thyrotoxicosis, acromegaly — not Cushing's. (Book p855)

items.q: ‘The m/c cause of panic attack is NOT pheochromocytoma.’
items.exp: Note: m/c cause of panic attack is not pheochromocytoma (though panic attack occurs in 75% of pheo patients). (Book p855)

items.q: The histopathology pattern of pheochromocytoma is the ___.
Before biochemical testing, which drugs must be stopped because they interfere?
items.exp: Stop tricyclic antidepressants, L-Dopa and NSAIDs before testing (they interfere with the test). (Book p855)
